procedural_matters: Hearing No. 2, 3 and 5 was heard together in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since all the hearings arose from the same incident.

During the hearing of a valid protests no. 2 and no. 3 International Jury learned that boats CRO 8280 and GER 8515 were involved in the same incident and that they may broke a rule. International Jury closed the hearing of protests no. 2 and no. 3, lodged the protest against boats CRO 8280 and GER 8515 and call a new hearing.
GER 8515 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).

Tracking evidence form Vakaros Race Sense system (official tracking system of the event) was presented. Vakaros Race Sense provides boat position 5 times per second with accuracy 25-30 cm and shows the boat size and zone size in the same scale. (This can be seen in the Race Viewer for Race 2 from time stamp T+ 54.15)
facts: Wind speed around 8 knots with choppy waves.
AUT 8407, GER 8515, AUT 7857, GER 8384 and CRO 8280 were on the run approaching starboard leeward gate mark.
AUT 8407 on port tack inside overlapped 3/4 of boat length ahead of GER 8515 on port tack entered the zone first.
AUT 7857 inside, GER 8384 in the middle and CRO 8280 outside were all on port tack, all overlapped, all clear astern of GER 8515 and AUT 8407.

Before AUT 8407 came abreast of the mark two boat lengths from it GER 8515 gybed, still outside the zone and slightly luffed. When GER 8515 reached the zone she was still overlapped with AUT 8407 inside and clear ahead of AUT 7857, GER 8384 and CRO

At the same time CRO 8280 gybed to starboard. Immediately after GER 8515 entered the zone AUT 7857 on port tack entered the zone. She was still overlapped with GER 8384 in the middle on port tack and with CRO 8280 outside.

AUT 8407 gybed to starboard and remain overlapped inside GER 8515. AUT 7857 inside on port, GER 8384 in the middle on port and CRO 8280 outside on starboard now all in the zone were in converging courses.

AUT 8407 now clear ahead of GER 8515 luffed towards the mark when she was abreast of the mark at the distance two boat lengths to it. GER 8515 also creIated overlapp with AUT 7857, GER 8384 and CRO 8280.
CRO 8280 bore away and AUT 7857 luffed slightly. CRO 8280, GER 8384 and AUT 7857 now sailed on the parallel courses less than 30 cm to each other.
AUT 7857 and GER 8384 gybed to starboard.

When AUT 8407 luffed more towards the mark, GER 8515 luffed also and established inside overlapp with AUT 8407. AUT 7857, GER 8384 and CRO 8280 luffed slightly. Now all other boats were sailing into the gap between AUT 8407 and the mark.
When distance between CRO 8280 and GER 8515 diminished GER 8515 bore away towards AUT 8407.

When AUT 8407 rounded the the mark, she was less than half boat length from it and contact occurred between bow of AUT 7857 and mid starboard side of the hull of AUT 8407 and between bow of GER 8384 and aft third starboard side of the hull of AUT 8407. There was also a contact side by side between hulls of GER 8384 and CRO 8280 and side by side contact between CRO 8280 and GER 8515 and side by side between GER 8515 bow and hull of AUT 8407.
After the incident GER 8384 and AUT 7857 took a one turn penalties.

Contact between AUT 8407, AUT 7857 and GER 8384 caused gel-coat damage on AUT 8407 hull. Other contacts didn't cause any damage on the boats. Case 2 Star Wolrds 2025. mov 17.5 MB Case 2 Star Wolrds 2025 with floating sail numbers. mov 32.8 MB diagram#2. jpg 86.1 KB
conclusions: When changing course, AUT 8407 the right-of-way boat failed to give GER 8515 room to keep clear, and broke RRS 16.1.
Since AUT 8407 broke RRS 16 while she was sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.

When it became clear that GER 8515 was not keeping clear and not giving mark-room it was reasonably possible for AUT 8407, the right-of-way boat and the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, to avoid contact with GER 8515. AUT 8407 broke RRS 14(a).

Since AUT 8407 was right-of way boat and sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled and the contact did not cause damage or injury, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(c) for breaking RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for AUT 8407, the right-of-way boat and the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, to avoid contact with GER 8384 and AUT 7857 when it became clear that both boates were not keeping clear and not giving mark-room. AUT 8407 did not break RRS 14(a). B - CRO 8280
CRO 8280 to windward failed to keep clear of GER 8515 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
CRO 8280 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give GER 8384 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
CRO 8280 not overlapped with AUT 8407 and not in the zone at the time AUT 8407 reached the zone, failed to give AUT 8407 mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
CRO 8280 not overlapped with GER 8515 and not in the zone at the time GER 8515 reached the zone, failed to give GER 8515mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
CRO 8280 did not avoid contact with GER 8515 and with GER 8384 when it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14. C - GER 8384
GER 8384 to windward failed to keep clear of CRO 8280 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
GER 8384 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give AUT 7857 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
GER 8384 not overlapped with AUT 8407 and not in the zone at the time AUT 8407 reached the zone, failed to give AUT 8407 mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
GER 8384 not overlapped with GER 8515 and not in the zone at the time GER 8515 reached the zone, failed to give GER 8515 mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
Since GER 8384 was compelled to break RRS 11, 18.2(a)(1) and 18.2(a)(2) as a consequence of CRO 8280 breaking RRS 18.2(a)(1), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breaches.

It was not reasonably possible for GER 8384 the right-of-way boat and boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with AUT 8407, AUT 7857 and CRO 8280 when it became clear that CRO 8280 is not giving mark-room. GER 8384 did not break RRS 14. D - AUT 7857
AUT 7857 to windward failed to keep clear of GER 8384 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
AUT 7857 not overlapped with AUT 8407 and not in the zone at the time AUT 8407 reached the zone, failed to give AUT 8407 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
AUT 7857 not overlapped with GER 8515 and not in the zone at the time GER 8515 reached the zone, failed to give GER 8515 mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
Since AUT 7857 was compelled to break RRS 11, 18.2(a)(2) as a consequence of CRO 8280 breaking RRS 18.2(a)(1), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.

It was not reasonably possible for AUT 7857 the boat sailing within the room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with GER 8383 and AUT 8407 when it became clear that CRO 8280 is not giving mark-room. AUT 7857 did not break RRS 14. E - GER 8515
GER 8515 to windward failed to keep clear of AUT 8407 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
GER 8515 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give AUT 8407 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
Since GER 8515 was compelled to break RRS 11 and 18.2(a)(1) as a consequence of CRO 8280 breaking RRS 11 and 18.2(a)(2), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breaches.

It was not reasonably possible for AUT 8407 the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with AUT 7857, GER 8384 and GER 8515 when it became clear that they are not giving mark-room. AUT 8407 did not break RRS 14.

It was not reasonably possible for GER 8515 the right-of-way boat and boat sailing within mark-room to which she was entitle to avoid contact with AUT 8407 and with CRO 8280 when it became clear that CRO 8280 is not keeping clear and giving mark-room.
decision: CRO 8280 is DSQ in race no. 2
